chapter: Bird's world, singers and the new music
title: Billy Eckstine's band at the Regal
summary: He lists the personnel and calls it the greatest band he played with.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: We did talk about the Eckstine band earlier on. But are there any other memories of that band that come to mind?

Oh, man. That was the greatest band I ever played with in my life, the band that Billy Eckstine had at the Regal Theatre in Chicago. They had Charlie Parker, Lucky Thompson, Dexter Gordon, Leo Parker, and who else was there... The trumpets, they had me and Dizzy, Shorts, and
Brockman. And they had four trombones -- Bennie Green, Gus Chappell...
Was Jerry Valentine there at the time?
Yeah, Jerry Valentine, he was there. And another little guy was there.
Chippie Outcault, he was there, too. Oh, it was a helluva band, man...
And Art Blakey. Tommy Potter, was he there?
Yeah, Art Blakey was there, Tommy Potter, and John Malachi -- and B. And they had this little guitar player, too.
Yeah, he was there, in the band. We had a helluva band, though, man.
Well, who was singing with the band with B, though? Sarah had gone?
Sarah was there. I'll tell you, that was some band!

Yeah, talking about Billy Eckstine's band. Pshew! That was some band. I'm telling you, I never played with a band that played any more than they did. Because I think that they had about the best musicians that I knew of at the

time. Maybe not in all sections, but I mean, they had one that could stand up with anybody. And Billy Eckstine, I think he could just sing as well any sum bitch I ever heard sing, you know. I don't know why the band couldn't hang together, but B said he couldn't put enough people to make the band pay off. I guess that kind of blew his (?), too.
